patterns.title: Private batch speech analytics with a separate model lifecycle
patterns.use_when: Private batch audio processing with transcription, masking, scoring and model inference; reference for structure, not a mandatory stack.
patterns.avoid: Do not copy the customer name, Mumbai region, instance families, models, two-AZ sizing, retention or existing dashboards into other projects. The picture is a user reference, not AWS-verified architecture. Treat schedule arrows as orchestration control, not audio transfer.
patterns.flow: Customer-owned recordings -> landing object store -> transcription compute -> masking/scoring compute <-> model inference -> results store -> existing consumer. Model training -> approved model registry -> deployment is a separate lifecycle, with container images distinct from model artifacts.
patterns.layout: Clear customer/sandbox ownership boundaries; private workload subnets inside VPC; regional S3 and orchestration outside subnets; public egress above workloads only when required. Main batch path centrally, model lifecycle in a lower band, security/monitoring in a compact separate band. Do not connect shared controls merely for appearance.
deployment_checks: Identify private compute and required service endpoints
Separate approved download egress from network-isolated training
Show AZ redundancy only when selected in the project design
Place NAT in public subnets and compute in private subnets where applicable
Distinguish orchestration control from transcript transfer
anchors: KreditBee SLM Platform and Batch Call Analytics POC

patterns.title: Asynchronous job workers
patterns.use_when: Queue-backed work that outlives an HTTP request.
patterns.avoid: Do not use for a simple synchronous lookup.
patterns.flow: API → submitter → queue → worker; worker updates job state; client queries status.
patterns.layout: Keep queue and workers on the main job path; notifications branch from completion; image registry and monitoring belong to supporting controls.

patterns.title: Transactional events
patterns.use_when: Reliable propagation of committed business changes.
patterns.avoid: Do not introduce event infrastructure for ordinary CRUD alone.
patterns.flow: Business update and outbox commit together; change capture → event bus → consumer queue → projection.
patterns.layout: Show producer and consumer ownership separately; relational CDC and database streams are alternatives.

patterns.title: External asynchronous API callback
patterns.use_when: A remote job returns later through a callback.
patterns.avoid: Do not model a synchronous API as a long-running workflow.
patterns.flow: Workflow submits queued request → external job; callback endpoint → correlation lookup → waiting workflow resumes.
patterns.layout: Keep outbound submission and callback lanes distinct; preserve correlation and timeout handling.

patterns.title: GraphQL application backend
patterns.use_when: A selected GraphQL interface resolves multiple backend resources.
patterns.avoid: Do not add GraphQL to an existing REST-only contract.
patterns.flow: Authenticated client → GraphQL API → selected resolver → data or application backend.
patterns.layout: Authentication supports ingress; optional private backend integration is separate from managed API placement.

patterns.title: Parallel API composition
patterns.use_when: One response requires independent service calls.
patterns.avoid: Do not chain independent services or introduce parallelism for dependent steps.
patterns.flow: Ingress → orchestrator → independent services; results → aggregator → caller.
patterns.layout: Draw fan-out and merge; caches and circuit breakers are conditional, not mandatory nodes.

patterns.title: Search-backed application
patterns.use_when: Indexed search selects records from a separate source of truth.
patterns.avoid: Do not treat the search index as the transactional authority.
patterns.flow: Client → query service → search index; selected keys → system of record. Change ingestion updates the index separately.
patterns.layout: Separate online queries from indexing; optional query enrichment must be justified.

patterns.title: Recorded audio processing
patterns.use_when: Uploaded recordings require transcription or text analysis.
patterns.avoid: Not a live telephony architecture; excluded voice remains excluded.
patterns.flow: Audio storage → transcription job → transcript storage → selected text analysis.
patterns.layout: Keep language translation and downstream analytics optional; do not invent a contact centre.

patterns.title: Media content moderation
patterns.use_when: A delivered feature checks uploaded media.
patterns.avoid: Do not add every media modality or model training.
patterns.flow: Media ingestion → modality-specific analysis → decision storage; uncertain items may route to human review.
patterns.layout: Branch by actual media type; human review and training labels are distinct optional paths.

patterns.title: Parallel model inference
patterns.use_when: Independent deployed models process the same job.
patterns.avoid: Internal reasoning steps do not justify multiple model deployments.
patterns.flow: Authenticated API → job storage → workflow fan-out → model endpoints → results; status API reads results.
patterns.layout: Separate job control from model execution and results access.

patterns.title: Document to speech
patterns.use_when: Document content is explicitly delivered as audio.
patterns.avoid: Do not add speech or translation to ordinary document extraction.
patterns.flow: Client uploads document → workflow → text extraction → selected language processing → speech synthesis → audio storage.
patterns.layout: Show upload and download paths; omit optional translation when unnecessary.

patterns.title: Selected AWS contact centre
patterns.use_when: Amazon Connect is explicitly selected for contact-centre delivery.
patterns.avoid: Existing Genesys or another agent platform is not permission to replace it.
patterns.flow: Customer → contact routing → human agent; routing or agent application calls required business APIs.
patterns.layout: Keep recordings and analytics on supporting branches; preserve external CRM ownership.

patterns.title: Real-time backend for frontend
patterns.use_when: Clients need event-driven updates and a tailored read model.
patterns.avoid: Do not add persistent connections for ordinary request-response pages.
patterns.flow: Domain events → consumer → read model; client → query API → read model; changes → push handler → connected client.
patterns.layout: Separate read path, connection registry and push path.

patterns.title: Centralized log analytics
patterns.use_when: Centralized log analysis is an actual delivery requirement.
patterns.avoid: Routine monitoring alone does not justify an analytics platform.
patterns.flow: Log producers → storage → notification queue → transform → search index → dashboards.
patterns.layout: Use a side lane; business requests do not pass through logging services.

patterns.title: Protected external origin
patterns.use_when: A CDN fronts a selected external web origin.
patterns.avoid: Do not invent an external origin or credential rotation workflow.
patterns.flow: Client → CDN associated with web ACL → protected origin.
patterns.layout: WAF is an associated control, not a separate application hop; origin protection is distinct from viewer authentication.

patterns.title: Device telemetry ingestion
patterns.use_when: Devices publish operational telemetry.
patterns.avoid: Do not add devices or legacy analytics products to an ordinary web application.
patterns.flow: Device → MQTT broker → routing rule → operational store; API reads stored telemetry.
patterns.layout: Separate device ingress and application queries; use only currently selected analytics capabilities.

patterns.title: Hybrid and partner file ingestion
patterns.use_when: On-premises or partner files enter cloud storage.
patterns.avoid: Do not mandate both private connectivity and internet transfer.
patterns.flow: On-premises files → transfer service → object storage; partner SFTP is an alternative ingress.
patterns.layout: Show ownership boundaries; processing branches and specialist file systems require separate justification.

patterns.title: Grounded knowledge retrieval
patterns.use_when: Answers must use a selected document knowledge source.
patterns.avoid: Not every chatbot needs a vector store; select one supported retrieval implementation.
patterns.flow: Documents → chunking and embeddings → retrieval index; query → retriever → relevant passages → answer model.
patterns.layout: Separate offline ingestion from online answering; managed retrieval and custom orchestration are alternatives.

patterns.title: Tool-using agent runtime
patterns.use_when: An agent invokes permitted tools through a selected runtime.
patterns.avoid: Do not replace an agreed runtime or add every AgentCore capability.
patterns.flow: Caller → agent runtime; runtime invokes model and authorized tools; tool results return to the runtime.
patterns.layout: Model and tools are runtime dependencies, not a fabricated serial chain; memory and gateways are optional.

patterns.title: Container application ingress
patterns.use_when: A container workload needs an inbound application interface.
patterns.avoid: Do not stack ALB, NLB and API Gateway by default.
patterns.flow: Client → selected ingress → container service → required dependencies.
patterns.layout: An ALB belongs to one VPC across selected subnets, not between VPCs; private tasks and managed services have different boundaries.

patterns.title: Asynchronous document extraction
patterns.use_when: Document analysis needs an asynchronous job lifecycle.
patterns.avoid: Do not route already structured records through OCR.
patterns.flow: Stored document → start analysis; completion topic → queue or handler → fetch analysis results.
patterns.layout: Separate job submission, completion notification and result retrieval; notification targets are alternatives.
